parte: Part V · What you have, what you produce, who works · phases 4–6

blocuri.text: Stocktaking is the moment when accounting admits it can be wrong. All the other checks in this book compare figures against other figures; this one compares figures against the world — actually counting what is in the warehouse, in the cash register, in the business.

It is also the only accounting operation that cannot be done from an office. Someone has to go, count, and write down what they found. That is precisely why it is required by law, at least once a year, before the financial statements are prepared.
Why differences appear even when no one is stealing
The first reaction to an inventory shortfall is suspicion. Most of the time, the explanation is more mundane and worth knowing, because it completely changes how it should be treated.

randuri: book (recorded) shortage — the goods really did leave
book (recorded) shortage — the goods never actually came in twice
actual shortage, cause to be determined
blocuri.nota: The first two are not shortages: they are recording errors, and treating them as shortages hides the real problem.

blocuri.text: That is why the correct order for an inventory result is: first look for recording errors, then establish the shortage. A shortage recorded as a loss, when in fact a delivery note was missing, "resolves" the difference and leaves behind an unbilled sale.
How the result is recorded
Once the actual differences have been established, they are recorded, and the accounting treatment is brief and worth knowing.

randuri: the company has more than it knew — recorded as revenue
the shortage becomes an expense of the company
the company has a receivable from the person responsible, including VAT
blocuri.nota: The third situation is the only one where VAT appears: recovery from the custodian is, for tax purposes, a taxable transaction.

blocuri.text: Charging the shortage to someone is neither automatic nor mandatory. It presupposes that liability has been established — which requires procedure, not just a difference on a table. A shortage charged without grounds quickly turns into a labor dispute that the company loses.
Stocktaking does not end with a figure, but with a minutes report: what was counted, what came out differently, and what was decided for each difference.
What is actually inventoried

The word evokes the warehouse, but stocktaking concerns the entire patrimony. Goods and materials are counted, but the cash register and balances with partners are also verified — through confirmation requests — and the physical existence of fixed assets is checked.

This last part is the one most often skipped, and the most instructive. A company that inventories its fixed assets often discovers equipment scrapped long ago that is still on the books and still being depreciated — or, conversely, equipment used daily and never recorded.

The general inventory of assets, liabilities, and equity items is mandatory at least once during the financial year, and the results are recorded in the inventory register; the rules on organizing and carrying out stocktaking establish the composition of the committee, the procedure for custodian declarations, how listings are prepared, and the treatment of surpluses and shortages. Offsetting surpluses against shortages is allowed only under strict limits — for the same custody period, between confusable product types, within quantity limits, and with written justification — and cannot be used as a general method of smoothing differences. For non-chargeable shortages related to goods for which VAT was deducted, adjustment of the tax is mandatory under Art. 304-305 of the Fiscal Code, except for technological losses within established limits; omitting this adjustment is one of the most common findings in VAT audits. Valuation at stocktaking is done at inventory value, and a decrease in value compared to cost — without physical shortage — is reflected through impairment adjustments, not by removal from the records.
What comes next
With stocktaking, the section on things comes to a close. Next comes the section on people: payroll, the most heavily regulated monthly operation in all of accounting.

blocuri.titlu: Exercise 20.1 — surplus and shortage in the same stocktaking
enunt: At stocktaking, for the same custody, a surplus of 12 units of product A (cost 40 lei/unit) and a shortage of 15 units of product B (cost 30 lei/unit) are found.
(a) Are they offset? (b) What is recorded?
rezolvare: (a) As a rule, no. Offsetting surpluses against shortages is allowed only between confusable product types, from the same group, within quantity limits, and with justification — not as a method to make the total come out even.
(b) The surplus: 12 × 40 = 480 lei, recorded as an increase in stock, offset against operating revenue.

The shortage: 15 × 30 = 450 lei, is removed from stock as an expense. If chargeable, it is charged to the custodian at the charging value, plus related output VAT. If non-chargeable, the VAT deducted on purchase is adjusted.

What is lost through offsetting: 480 − 450 = 30 lei might seem "almost nothing." But offsetting hides TWO real problems — an unrecorded inflow and an unrecorded outflow — and next month both will repeat, because no one looked for the cause.

blocuri.text: The procedure, because without it the result cannot be defended

Stocktaking has a form set out in regulations, and the form is not bureaucracy: it is the only thing that turns a count into evidence. A shortage found without procedure cannot be charged to anyone, and a surplus cannot be justified during an audit.

randuri: names the committee, the period, the custodies
without it, no one knows who is responsible for the count
they declare that all documents have been handed over
they are the primary document of the operation
this is where surpluses and shortages appear
the causes and the committee's proposals
only now is accounting actually touched
blocuri.nota: The custodian's declaration is given BEFORE counting, not after. If given after, it could be adjusted to match what came out.

blocuri.text: The order has a logic worth seeing: the first three stages produce facts, the fourth produces differences, the fifth produces explanations, and only the sixth touches the figures. Whoever jumps straight to the last one ends up with entries lacking a written reason — exactly what cannot be defended two years later.
Offsets and natural loss allowances
Two mechanisms reduce differences before they are recorded, and both apply restrictively, not as a method to make the total come out even.

Offsetting surpluses against shortages is allowed only between confusable product types, from the same group, within the smaller quantities, and only if the committee justifies the confusion. It is not a leveling of the total: two different products that cancel out in value remain two distinct problems.

Natural loss allowances cover the normal losses from handling, transport, or storage — evaporation, breakage, drying — within limits set by government decision, by category of goods. They are granted only upon finding an actual shortage and only up to the legal limit: beyond it, the rest remains a chargeable or non-chargeable shortage.
Neither offsetting nor natural loss allowance explains a shortage. They only acknowledge that part of it was foreseeable. The rest requires an answer.
Not just inventory (stock)
The word "inventory" evokes the warehouse, but the obligation concerns the entire patrimony: fixed assets, receivables, liabilities, cash, even items held in off-balance-sheet accounts.

Stocktaking of receivables is not done by counting, but by confirmation: the partner is asked to confirm the balance. This is the procedure that uncovers invoices they never received, payments allocated incorrectly, and receivables that no longer exist. For fixed assets, the count confirms that the item on the register still physically exists — and for undeclared write-offs, that is where they turn up.

The result of the entire operation is recorded in the inventory register, which is a mandatory register, alongside the journal ledger and the general ledger. Without it, financial statements are prepared on figures that were never checked against reality.

puncte: Stocktaking is the only check that compares figures against the world, not against other figures. It is mandatory annually, before the balance sheet.
Most differences are recording errors, not shortages. Documents are searched for first, then the shortage is established.
The surplus is recorded as revenue; the non-chargeable shortage becomes an expense; the chargeable one creates a receivable from the custodian, including VAT.
Charging someone presupposes liability established through procedure, not just a difference on a table.
The entire patrimony is inventoried, not just the warehouse — including fixed assets, where the biggest surprises appear.
